subject: Proof of local deletion & handover manifest for Private VPC tenant
messages:
From: Anna Rutherford <anna.rutherford@medicorehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Cc: legalops@medicorehealth.com
Date: 2027-09-28T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Evidence of deletion for tenant 'medicore-prod' (offboarding)

Hi Karthik,

We completed an offboarding for the tenant 'medicore-prod' in our Private VPC last week. Our compliance team needs an evidence package showing that:

- Active objects and snapshots in the customer-controlled storage were deleted or tombstoned.
- Any persistent backups or replica snapshots are scheduled for removal per your retention policy.
- Key-management/crypto steps taken (e.g., KMS key rotation/revocation) to ensure data is inaccessible.

Can Redwood provide a signed attestation and a timestamped manifest listing erased object IDs and timestamps? If there are limitations (e.g., backups outside immediate control), please call them out so we can map to our retention policy.

Thanks,
Anna Rutherford
Head of Security Operations
Medicore Health

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
To: Anna Rutherford <anna.rutherford@medicorehealth.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: 2027-09-28T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Evidence of deletion for tenant 'medicore-prod' (offboarding)

Hi Anna — thanks for the note and context. We can produce an evidence package; a few clarifying points so we scope it correctly:

1) Scope: do you want artifacts for object-level deletions in customer-controlled storage only, or also control-plane metadata (snapshots, index records) that our control plane may retain briefly for operational rollback?
2) Time window: confirm the deletion window you need (e.g., deleted between 2027-09-20 and 2027-09-26).
3) Legal hold: any outstanding holds or eDiscovery requests we should be aware of?

Technical team — looping in Prio (Priyom) and Marissa to draft the manifest format we usually provide (object ID, bucket/path, deletion timestamp, tombstone flag, retention-expiry).

We will attach a preliminary manifest and a draft attestation for Medicore to review.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das@redwood.example.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: 2027-09-28T19:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Evidence of deletion for tenant 'medicore-prod' (offboarding) — tech details

Notes for the manifest and attestation:

- We can produce an object-level CSV (erase_manifest_20270929.csv) with columns: object_id, storage_path, last_write_ts, deletion_ts, tombstone (true/false), tombstone_reason, snapshot_id_parent, retention_expiry_ts, responsible_node_id.
- For private/VPC deployments using customer-controlled storage (S3-compatible buckets in the customer's VPC), deletion is performed via a signed job executed on the customer's control plane connectors that call the customer's object API. We record the job output and the API responses in our audit log.
- Backups: if the customer had cross-region replication or a third-party backup agent, Redwood only controls objects it wrote to the customer-controlled store. We'll flag replicas that we did NOT delete and provide guidance.
- Crypto: for tenants using Redwood-managed KMS proxies we can provide key-rotation logs and a record of CMK status changes. For customer-managed KMS in their VPC, we provide attestations that deletion API calls were issued; we cannot revoke customer-managed keys.
- For stronger guarantees we offer signed manifests with a SHA256 integrity digest and a separate signed attestation PDF (procedure_flow_tombstone_v1.pdf attached) explaining the workflow and limitations.

I can generate the CSV and a preliminary digest by EOD and hand it to Legal for signature.

— Prio
Senior Infra Engineer, Data Stewardship

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
To: Anna Rutherford <anna.rutherford@medicorehealth.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
Date: 2027-09-29T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Evidence of deletion for tenant 'medicore-prod' (offboarding) — preliminary package

Hi Anna — attaching the preliminary evidence package for Medicore's review:

- erase_manifest_20270929.csv (object IDs, deletion timestamps, tombstone flags)
- procedure_flow_tombstone_v1.pdf (technical description of deletion flow and limitations)

Summary items to call out in the package:
- Objects written to Medicore-managed buckets: deleted via the customer's object API at 2027-09-25T22:13:41Z; API response 204 logged.
- Two snapshot replicas flagged as outside Redwood's control because they were created by a third-party export agent; we have listed their snapshot IDs and owners in the CSV.
- KMS: Medicore used a customer-managed KMS key; we issued delete calls for objects but cannot revoke the CMK. We attach the KMS log lines showing the delete operations.

Next steps: if this looks good, our Legal team will apply a signature attestation PDF and provide a DocuSign wrapper. Laura — can you please review and produce the signed-attestation-karthik-20270930.pdf?

Action item for Medicore: confirm you accept the scope and note any additional buckets or cross-account replicas to include.

Best,
Karthik

From: Anna Rutherford <anna.rutherford@medicorehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Cc: legalops@medicorehealth.com
Date: 2027-09-29T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Evidence of deletion for tenant 'medicore-prod' (offboarding) — preliminary package

Karthik — thanks for the quick turnaround and the CSV. A couple of follow-ups:

- Please include a SHA256 digest of the CSV and sign the digest (we will store the manifest in our evidence vault).
- We need an explicit flag in the manifest for any object that is part of a point-in-time snapshot chain (so we can map to our retention ledger).
- On the two replicas you flagged: please add contact points for the owners/operators so we can follow up.

If Legal can sign an attestation that calls out the exact scope and the two external replica exceptions, we can close the offboarding ticket.

Appreciate it —
Anna

From: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
To: Anna Rutherford <anna.rutherford@medicorehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, priyom_das@redwood.example.com
Date: 2027-09-30T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Signed attestation: Medicore 'medicore-prod' deletion evidence

Anna — attaching the signed attestation PDF (signed-attestation-karthik-20270930.pdf) and the CSV digest. The attestation explicitly states scope: objects deleted from customer-controlled storage under 'medicore-prod' between 2027-09-20T00:00:00Z and 2027-09-26T23:59:59Z, and enumerates the two replica snapshot IDs that Redwood did not delete because they are owned by a third-party export agent.

Keynotes in the attestation:
- We include a SHA256 digest of erase_manifest_20270929.csv and a corresponding signature block.
- We document KMS limitations for customer-managed keys and include KMS operation logs showing delete requests.
- We provide a recommended remediation for the replicas: contact details and a suggested export/handback process so Medicore can assert deletion on those replicas.

DocuSign record: https://app.docusign.com/records/ABC-DEF-20270930
Drive folder with artifacts: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C/medicore-erase-manifests

If you need our compliance team to run a short attestation call for your auditors, we're happy to schedule.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
